claims.claim: When k=2, a vertex is uniquely determined by its support.
claims.evidence: Nonnegative integer coordinates summing to two have either one positive coordinate equal to two, or two positive coordinates both equal to one. Thus singleton support {i} determines 2e_i, and two-element support {i,j} determines e_i+e_j. These exhaust every n≥1.
claims.search_method: Complete integer case analysis; supplementary enumeration of all 36 vertices at n=8.

claims.claim: For k=2 and distinct a,b, the landmark e_a+e_b measures the sum of the support indicators at a and b.
claims.evidence: The identity |u−v|=u+v−2min(u,v), summed over coordinates of two vertices of total mass two, gives d(x,r)=2−Σ_i min(x_i,r_i). For r=e_a+e_b this is 2−1_{x_a>0}−1_{x_b>0}. The checker independently confirmed all 1,008 vertex/pair-landmark measurements at n=8 using BFS distances.
claims.search_method: Symbolic derivation from the source metric; exhaustive exact comparison with token-move BFS.

claims.claim: On a block consisting of one center and at least three leaves, the center–leaf landmarks recover every support of size at most two within that block.
claims.evidence: For L≥3 leaves, a support without the center produces its leaf indicator vector, containing at most two ones. The center alone produces L ones. The center together with leaf j produces all ones with entry j increased to two. These classes are disjoint, and each vector identifies the support within its class. This proves injectivity for every L≥3, including the empty local support.
claims.witness: For three leaves, the eleven overlap vectors are 000, 100, 010, 001, 110, 101, 011, 111, 211, 121, 112.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive symbolic classification by center membership; exact local enumeration for three through six leaves.

claims.evidence: Write n=4q+r with q≥1 and 0≤r≤3. Partition the coordinates into q−1 blocks of size four and one of size 4+r. Each block contributes its size minus one distinct admissible center–leaf landmarks, totaling n−q. Every local support has size at most two and is recovered by claim 2. The recovered global support determines the vertex by claim 0. This covers all n≥4 and all vertices.
claims.witness: Partition into block sizes 4,...,4,4+r and select every center–leaf pair within each block.
claims.search_method: Complete partition and decoding proof; supplementary exact construction checks for n=4 through 16.

claims.claim: For n=8 and k=2, six explicit admissible landmarks resolve all 36 vertices.
claims.evidence: Independently enumerated all 36 nonnegative integer eight-vectors of sum two and verified all six landmarks are distinct members. Constructed adjacency by individual token transfers and computed every distance by BFS. All 1,296 distances agree with the source formula. The six-landmark signatures are distinct for all 36 vertices, separating all 630 unordered pairs; local decoding also reconstructs every vertex.
claims.witness: n=8, k=2; R={e_1+e_2,e_1+e_3,e_1+e_4,e_5+e_6,e_5+e_7,e_5+e_8}, where e_i is the ith standard basis vector in eight coordinates.
claims.search_method: Complete finite integer enumeration, independently constructed token-move BFS, signature comparison, and explicit decoding.

claims.claim: Represent any resolving set R for k=2 by a simple graph H of pair landmarks and a marked set M of double landmarks. If H has an unmarked isolated vertex, then |R|≥n−1.
claims.evidence: Every landmark is uniquely a pair landmark or a double landmark, so |R|=|E(H)|+|M|. Let i be isolated and unmarked. If another coordinate j is unmarked, compare 2e_j with e_i+e_j. No pair landmark contains i; its overlap with either vertex is one exactly when it contains j. Every double landmark is outside {i,j} and has overlap zero with both. Thus the two distinct vertices have identical distances to every landmark. Resolution therefore forces all n−1 other coordinates to be marked.
claims.witness: The collision forced by two such unmarked coordinates is x=2e_j and y=e_i+e_j.
claims.search_method: Complete analysis of both landmark types; supplementary exact collision checks for all ordered i≠j at n=8.

claims.claim: An unmarked tree component of H cannot have two or three vertices when R resolves F_2(K_n).
claims.evidence: A two-vertex tree is one edge ij: 2e_i and 2e_j each have overlap one with that edge landmark. A three-vertex tree is a path a−b−c: 2e_b and e_a+e_c each have overlap one with both edge landmarks. Since the component is unmarked and has no edges to other components, every remaining landmark has overlap zero with both vertices in the respective collision. Neither component can occur in a resolving set.
claims.witness: Two-vertex collision: 2e_i versus 2e_j. Three-vertex path collision: 2e_b versus e_a+e_c.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive classification of trees on two and three vertices; exact checks against every allowed outside landmark at n=8.

claims.claim: For every n≥4, every resolving set for F_2(K_n) has at least n−⌊n/4⌋ landmarks.
claims.evidence: If an unmarked isolated coordinate exists, claim 5 gives |R|≥n−1≥n−⌊n/4⌋. Otherwise, claims 5–6 exclude unmarked tree components of sizes one, two, and three. Let t count the remaining unmarked tree components; their disjoint vertex sets imply 4t≤n. A marked connected component on v vertices contributes at least v−1 edges and one mark, hence at least v landmarks. An unmarked cyclic component contributes at least v edges. Each unmarked tree contributes v−1 edges. These exhaustive component cases give |R|≥n−t≥n−⌊n/4⌋.
claims.witness: Component certificate: |R|≥n−t and 4t≤n when no unmarked isolated coordinate exists.
claims.search_method: Complete component-counting proof, including isolated, marked, cyclic, and unmarked tree components; independent exhaustive lower-bound check at n=8.

claims.claim: For every n≥4, dim(F_2(K_n))=n−⌊n/4⌋; in particular, dim(F_2(K_8))=6.
claims.evidence: The independently verified upper and lower bounds coincide for every n≥4. At n=8 they equal six. Additionally, the exact checker enumerated all binomial(36,5)=376,992 five-landmark subsets and recovered an indistinguishable vertex pair for every subset. Any smaller resolving set could be extended to five landmarks while preserving resolution, so none exists. Together with the explicit six-landmark set, this independently certifies dimension six.
claims.witness: At n=8, R={e_1+e_2,e_1+e_3,e_1+e_4,e_5+e_6,e_5+e_7,e_5+e_8}; exhaustive enumeration excludes every five-landmark subset.
claims.search_method: Matching universal proofs plus complete integer enumeration of every five-landmark candidate at n=8.

claims.evidence: The original assertion quantifies over all positive integers n,k. The instance n=8,k=2 satisfies its exact domain and uses precisely the specified nonnegative integer vertices and token-transfer adjacency. Its certified metric dimension is six, whereas the asserted value n−1 is seven. Even the independently verified upper bound six already contradicts the asserted equality. This is a counterexample to the original conjecture itself.
claims.search_method: Exact source-hypothesis comparison and complete finite counterexample certification using token-move BFS and exhaustive landmark enumeration.

target_evidence: The exact target asks whether dim(F_k(K_n))=n−1 holds for every n≥1,k≥1 and prioritizes an explicit exact counterexample. The draft supplies the admissible instance (n,k)=(8,2) and six explicit valid landmarks. Independent integer computations reconstructed the source graph, verified every distance, and established resolution of its complete 36-vertex set. Thus dim(F_2(K_8))≤6<7 already refutes the universal assertion with all hypotheses preserved. Exhaustive exclusion of every five-landmark subset also proves the stated exact dimension six. The general k=2 formula has a complete construction and component-counting proof. Consequently the draft's FULL resolution claim and refutation headline are accurate.
